Findings triage — **route repair: `domain:core` → `domain:engine-core`. `finding` grade unchanged, no ownership taken.**

- **Why the replacement**: `domain:core` is not in the SKILL domain-lane roster — no seat filter returns it, so the card was routed into a lane that does not exist (the exact ownerless-lane shape the vocabulary table warns about). The anchor is `packages/core/src/qa/runner.ts` — the `contains` case verified live at `:171-:177` on `origin/main` @ `397e731`, with no `else` branch, exactly as filed. `packages/core` is in the `domain:engine-core` package family. (Note: this is `packages/core`, not `packages/qa` — the latter would be `domain:cli`; the anchoring rule goes by the file.)
- **Grade kept, with a recorded promotion trigger**: the false-green shape (a `contains` assertion against a missing path reports ✅) is restore-invariant class, and option 1 (throw on the unhandled shape) is the only one that closes it. It stays `finding` today because the qa runner's consumer surface is only now coming alive — #6247/PR #7255 is enforcing `TestSuiteSchema` at the `os test` load site. **Restart condition: when PR #7255 lands and real suites run through this engine, promote to `pm:queue`** — at that point every falsely-green `contains` is a lie CI believes.
- Off-roster-label note for the roster: `domain:core` now has zero open uses again; it is not in the SKILL table and should not be re-applied — this is the retired-label pattern (`domain:engine`/`domain:ui`) with a new spelling.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Blast-radius measurement — the loud path is implemented and the radius is measured. PR #7348 (draft).** Session `session_01EdBxv9i73dqkDD2QcnvNzd` · branch `claude/issue-7256-qa-contains-silent-pass` · worktree `objectstack-7256`, base `f3f855ac`.

Option **1** taken (throw on the unhandled shape), per the card. Option 2 rejected for the reason the issue gives: `String(undefined).includes("defi")` trades one false green for a stranger one.

## In-tree radius: **zero vacuous cases**, with the run as evidence

`os test` is `TestRunner`'s only consumer in the repository (`packages/cli/src/commands/test.ts:130-131`), and there are no Quality Protocol suites for it to run.

**Run A — the default glob, on the loud build, from every place an app lives:**

```
$ node packages/cli/bin/run.js test          # default: qa/*.test.json
   repo root            → No test files found matching: qa/*.test.json   exit=0
   examples/app-showcase → No test files found matching: qa/*.test.json   exit=0
   examples/app-crm      → No test files found matching: qa/*.test.json   exit=0
   examples/app-todo     → No test files found matching: qa/*.test.json   exit=0
```

None of the three apps has a `qa/` directory at all; all three run `vitest run` for `pnpm test`.

**Run B — the repo-wide sweep.** Every `*.test.json` in the tree, `node_modules` excluded, is three `tsconfig.test.json` files (`packages/client`, `packages/metadata-core`, `packages/spec`). Fed to `os test` explicitly, each is refused at the load site by #6247's `TestSuiteSchema` parse (`is not valid JSON: Unexpected token '/'`) — they were never suites. The only JSON in the repo with a top-level `scenarios` key is `packages/spec/liveness/qa.json`, the ledger itself. No `.yml`/`.yaml` suite exists. `packages/qa/{dogfood,downstream-contract,http-conformance}` are vitest suites that never touch `TestRunner`. No workflow in `.github/workflows/` invokes `os test`.

> Side finding from Run B: `os test '**/*.test.json'` from a repo root **OOMs** — `resolveGlob` calls `readdirSync(baseDir, {recursive:true})` with `baseDir === '.'` and nothing prunes `node_modules`. Different file, so filed as **#7363** rather than folded.

**Run C — positive control**, because "zero suites" would otherwise be an untested claim about the loud path. Same fixture, same real `HttpTestAdapter`, against a stand-in server returning `{"ok":true,"data":{"total":0},"name":"acme corp","tags":["acme","globex"]}`:

| scenario | base `f3f855ac` | loud build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains` on `data.items` — path absent | ✅ *(asserting nothing)* | ❌ `got undefined` |
| `contains` on `body.data.items` — the **documented** `body.*` convention | ✅ *(asserting nothing)* | ❌ `got undefined` |
| `contains` on `data.total` — a number | ✅ *(asserting nothing)* | ❌ `got number` |
| `contains` on `tags` — a real array | ✅ | ✅ |
| `contains` on `name` — a real string | ✅ | ✅ |
| **suite verdict** | **`SUCCESS: All 5 scenarios passed.`** | **`FAILED: 3 scenarios failed. 2 passed.`** |

Exactly the three vacuous scenarios flip; both evaluable controls stay green. The base column is the bug in one line: a suite of five scenarios, three of which assert nothing, reporting all-green.

**So: no in-repo case was passing vacuously, none needed a fixture repair, and nothing relied on silent-pass as "field may be absent" semantics — there was no semantics decision to escalate.** Downstream suites are what will turn red, and every case they see is a test that was never running.

> The `body.data.items` row above is its own finding: `TestAssertionSchema.field` documents `"body.data.0.status"`, but `HttpTestAdapter` returns the parsed body with no `body` wrapper, so every documented path resolves to `undefined`. `equals` already failed loudly on it; `contains` passed. Filed as **#7365** — fixing it is a protocol call (correct the convention, or have the adapter return `{status, headers, body}`), not this cleanup.

## Sibling-operator sweep — same file, per the card

`contains` was the only type-switched assertion and the only one carrying this defect:

| operator | shape in `TestRunner.assert` | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `equals`, `not_equals` | unconditional compare | no hole |
| `is_null`, `not_null` | unconditional compare | no hole |
| `contains` | type-switched, **no `else`** | **the defect — fixed** |
| `not_contains`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `error` | declared in `TestAssertionTypeSchema`, no branch | already refused loudly at `default:` — the issue's "annoying but honest", not this defect |

`not_contains` exists in the schema; it does not carry the hole. The six declared-but-unimplemented operators are left alone — implementing them is a feature decision — and pinned in the new tests so a later implementation is deliberate.

## The message

Written so the author knows which of the two things is wrong. `undefined`/`null` ⇒ the path did not resolve, so the **fixture** is the suspect; anything else ⇒ the path resolved and the **assertion** picked an inapplicable operator. `null` and arrays are named as themselves, not `typeof`'s `object`.

```
Assertion failed: body.data.items cannot be evaluated by 'contains' — expected an
array or a string at that path, got undefined. The path resolved to nothing — the
field is absent from the result, or the path is misspelled. Use 'is_null' if
asserting absence is what you meant.
```

## Tests, changeset, gates

17 pins in a new `packages/core/src/qa/runner.test.ts`, driven through the public `runSuite` surface. Reverse-verified: reverting `runner.ts` alone fails 7 and passes the other 10, so the behaviour pins constrain the fix without over-constraining the unchanged paths. Full `@objectstack/core` suite green (744 tests / 30 files).

Changeset `@objectstack/core: minor`, read off `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: the whole monorepo versions in lockstep, so a `major` would promote all ~70 packages, and during the launch window breaking changes ship as `minor`. Not a `patch` — this changes published behaviour. `check-adr-0087-registration` confirms no disposition trio is needed; `packages/spec` is untouched.

Gate results are in the PR. One pre-existing red is worth naming here because it is this domain: **`check:platform-checklist` fails on untouched `f3f855ac`** — `coverage.json · qa: UNCLASSIFIED`, because #7255 seeded `packages/spec/liveness/qa.json` and the checklist has no `qa` row. Confirmed by running it in a second worktree at the base commit with no edits. Already filed as **#7347**; not mine to absorb.

**ACCEPT — PR #7348. Ready + queued (draft read back `False`, `mergeable_state: clean`).**

Verified against the brief by reading the report and the diff:

1. ✅ **The loud path names both the type and the fault line.** `describeActualType` distinguishes `null`/array/object where `typeof` lies, and `containsInapplicableHint` tells the author *which* of the two things is wrong: `undefined`/`null` ⇒ the fixture/path is the suspect (with an `is_null` pointer); anything else ⇒ the assertion picked an inapplicable operator (with `equals` guidance). That is exactly the "author knows whether their fixture or their assertion is wrong" bar.
2. ✅ **Blast radius measured three ways, not asserted**: Run A (default glob from repo root + all three example apps — no `qa/` dir anywhere, exit 0); Run B (repo-wide sweep — every `*.test.json` is a tsconfig, refused by #6247's schema at load; no YAML suites; no workflow invokes `os test`); Run C (**positive control** — the same fixture red on the loud build and green-while-asserting-nothing on base, so "zero vacuous cases" is itself a tested claim). In-tree radius: **zero**, proven.
3. ✅ Pins: 221 lines covering the three non-evaluable shapes loudly failing and both evaluable shapes' positive/negative behaviour unchanged.
4. ✅ **Side finding filed, not folded**: #7363 (`os test` with `**` glob OOMs — `resolveGlob` recurses `node_modules`), different file, verified open.
5. ✅ Changeset `minor` with the vacuous-green→red reasoning in the body; docs updated; 27 checks, 0 not-green.

Auto-merge armed; issue closes on merge.
